title: PRD: intake signal contract and rollback rules for unpinned open weights
creator: Leah Chen
description: This PRD clarifies the minimal intake signals and the decision contract for admitting new open-model weights to the catalog when we do NOT immediately pin a runtime version. The outcome should reduce ambiguity for runtime engineers and reduce risk of silent regressions for customers using unpinned community variants. The doc defines required metadata, runtime sanity probes, rollback triggers, and the lightweight acceptance checklist for ephemeral/experimental variants.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake form fields defined and validated: topology, tokenizer hash, recommended seq_len, supported activations, quantization hint, provenance and license URL.
A2: Compatibility tags taxonomy published (compat-level: high | partial | experimental) and mapped to runtime fallback behavior.
A3: Runtime sanity probe suite (3 smoke prompts + perf profile) implemented in ingest pipeline that runs on a canonical benchmark host within 24h of intake.
A4: Rollback rules documented: automatic soft-disable when 20% increase in downstream error traces or 40% throughput degradation observed for a pinned-route proxying this variant for >6h.
A5: Console UI surfaces variant compatibility and pinning recommendation on catalog entry page and flags unpinned variants in model selection endpoints.
A6: Security review checklist completed for PII/crypto concerns and security_review_required flagged for all unpinned community weights.
A7: Integration tests that verify fallback to pinned-compatible variant when variant fails sanity probes are added to runtime-acceptance CI.
A8: Documentation (Confluence PRD + onboarding checklist) published and linked from intake flow.
A9: Post-ingest monitoring dashboard (latency, 95p token time, token cost delta, quality drift via eval set) available to SRE and Catalog owners within 48h of ingestion.
A10: Stakeholder sign-off (Runtime, SRE, Security, Legal) recorded before public catalog exposure.
decisions: D1: Unpinned variants are allowed for exploratory catalog entries but must carry an explicit compat-level tag and an 'experimental' UI badge.
D2: Default runtime behavior for unpinned experimental variants is: route only from discovery/test routes and never default for production routes without manual opt-in.
D3: Automatic soft-disable is preferred to forced removal for initial failures to allow quick rollbacks while preserving forensic data.
D4: Minimal required intake metadata will be enforced by the intake API with server-side validation; missing fields reject the submission.
D5: Security review is mandatory for any unpinned model that declares a permissive license or unknown provenance.
D6: We will not require an immediate quantization profile at intake, but the intake must include quantization hints and tested numeric stability notes.
D7: A lightweight 'canary' traffic policy will be attached to all new unpinned variants for at least 72 hours.
D8: Acceptance gates are staged (ingest -> runtime smoke -> canary -> limited catalog exposure) and each stage must have clear rollback criteria.
D9: For documentation and auditability, all decisions and test outputs for the ingest run will be persisted under the catalog entry's audit log.
D10: We will surface a recommended 'pin' action for variants that pass the acceptance suite for two consecutive weeks of telemetry.
tradeoffs: T1: Stricter intake metadata increases onboarding friction for community contributors but reduces runtime foot-guns and support load.
T2: Immediate hard-pinning would raise operational burden and block many useful experimental weights; opting for soft-pinning balances agility vs safety.
T3: Running comprehensive numeric/regression tests at ingest would catch more issues but add cost and latency to acceptance; chosen probes are deliberately lightweight.
T4: Canary windows reduce blast radius but extend time-to-make-fully-available; we accept longer rollout for higher reliability.
T5: Mandating security review adds overhead but is necessary to limit compliance risk for enterprise customers.
